chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abi Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one performing Tamattu' who intended to shorten [his hair] but shaved his head. He said: 'Upon him is a blood offering [dam] which he pours [on his head]. And when it is the Day of Sacrifice (Yaw al-Nahr), he should run the razor over his head when he intends to shave.' If he had done that forgetfully, then there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood offering, a sacrificial animal required for certain ritual violations
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: To shorten [hair], the preferred act of shaving

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim shaves his head before the Day of Sacrifice during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific penalty for prematurely shaving during the Hajj of Tamattu', requiring the slaughter of a sheep (dam) as expiation. It distinguishes between intentional shaving, which incurs the penalty, and forgetful shaving, which is excused, reflecting the juristic principle of leniency in cases of unintentional error. The ruling underscores the ritual precision required in Hajj rites, linking physical acts of grooming directly to sacrificial obligations.
